```{r setup}
run <- "2026-10-09"
rd <- function(name) {
  p <- file.path("results", "barrier-ml", run, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  if (!file.exists(p)) stop("Missing ", p, ": run Rscript run_experiment.R")
  read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
tab <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), ...)
fam <- c(research47 = "research/47", engineering15 = "engineering/15", boomsma = "Boomsma 1985",
         wolf = "Wolf et al. 2013", chen = "Chen et al. 2001", constrained = "equality-constrained",
         ernst = "Ernst (control)")
arms <- c(default = "Default (FABIN3, PORT)", layered_port = "Layered, PORT",
          default_lbfgs = "FABIN3, L-BFGS", layered_lbfgs = "Layered, L-BFGS")
rates <- rd("rates_by_family"); rt <- rd("rates_by_family_transform")
choice <- rd("choice"); dec <- rd("decision"); loss <- rd("losses"); runaways <- rd("runaways")
f0 <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")
tot <- function(r, arm, col = "success", fams = NULL) sum(r[[col]][r$role == "test" & r$arm == arm &
  (is.null(fams) | r$family %in% fams)])
other <- setdiff(names(fam), c("constrained", "ernst"))
x001 <- function(arm) sum(rt$attainable[rt$role == "test" & rt$family == "constrained" &
  rt$transform == "x0.01" & rt$arm == arm] - rt$success[rt$role == "test" &
  rt$family == "constrained" & rt$transform == "x0.01" & rt$arm == arm])
lp <- loss[loss$role == "test" & loss$candidate == "layered_port", ]
lp_worse <- sum(is.finite(lp$fmin) & lp$fmin > lp$best_known + 1e-6 * (1 + abs(lp$best_known)))
lp_npc <- sum(lp$newton_status == "nonpositive_curvature")
ll <- loss[loss$role == "test" & loss$candidate == "layered_lbfgs", ]
dl <- loss[loss$role == "test" & loss$candidate == "default_lbfgs", ]
ls_fail <- function(d) sum(grepl("LineSearch", d$message))
pole <- function(arm) sum(runaways$chart_beyond_1000[runaways$role == "test" & runaways$arm == arm])
```

## Default register

| Default | Current value | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| barrier start | transported FABIN3 (pinned apart from the ML default) | settled: keep; neither layered arm is eligible | 2026-10-09, per-family rules in `decision.csv` |
| barrier optimizer | PORT | settled: keep; no L-BFGS candidate is eligible | 2026-10-09, per-family rules in `decision.csv` |
| barrier start at $\times 0.01$ in constrained models | native fallback built in normalized sample units | settled: units bug fixed by TASK-131; failures fell from 2,677 to `r f0(x001("default"))` | 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-09 |
| verdict at marker poles | same-endpoint std.lv Newton audit when transport is supported | settled for supported transports by TASK-137; equality-constrained transport remains open | certified chart extent > 1000: default 287 → `r f0(pole("default"))`, layered PORT 510 → `r f0(pole("layered_port"))`; exceptions discussed below |
| barrier weight $\lambda$ | 0.25 | not decided here; the sem-barrier paper owns it | none |
| FIML barrier start and optimizer | transported FABIN3, PORT | not covered | none |

## Question

Which start and optimizer should the complete-data ML barrier fitter
(`frontier_fit_ml_multiinfo`, latent-determinacy target with penalty
$\lambda \log\det Q$) use by default?
The [criteria](criteria/barrier-ml.md) were registered at `677e78bc`; the
fresh-seed rerun amendment was committed at `dd6325ad` before the run.

## Short answer

**Keep transported FABIN3 with PORT. No candidate is eligible.** After
TASK-131 and TASK-137, the default scores `r f0(choice$default_success[1])`
successful test fits, more than any candidate. Eligibility is judged separately
in every family at both weights, not by that total. The constrained-model
$\times 0.01$ start failure has been repaired. The supported marker-pole
verdict has been strengthened, but equality-constrained std.lv transport remains
unfinished, and a few certified high-extent cases remain outside that family.

## Findings: 2026-10-09

Successful fits among attainable problems, separately by family; the table
sums the two weights for display only. Success requires library certification
and both registered runaway bounds. Ernst is a development control and does
not gate the decision.

```{r by-family}
r <- rates[rates$arm %in% names(arms), ]
a <- aggregate(cbind(attainable, success) ~ role + family + arm, r, sum)
w <- reshape(a[c("role", "family", "arm", "success")], idvar = c("role", "family"),
             timevar = "arm", direction = "wide")
att <- a[a$arm == "default", c("role", "family", "attainable")]
w <- merge(att, w)
w <- w[order(w$role == "control", w$family), ]
out <- data.frame(Family = fam[w$family], Attainable = w$attainable,
                  lapply(names(arms), function(k) w[[paste0("success.", k)]]))
names(out)[-(1:2)] <- arms
tab(out)
```


Both layered arms fail the primary and best-known rules in Boomsma,
equality-constrained, engineering/15, research/47 and Wolf at both weights;
Chen ties. FABIN3 with L-BFGS fails these rules in equality-constrained,
engineering/15 and Wolf at both weights, and Boomsma at $\lambda=1$.
Its research/47 gains do not compensate for other families' losses.
Invariance also fails for each candidate in at least one registered scope.
The full per-weight rules remain in `decision.csv`.

Every loss against baseline is retained in `losses.csv`. The following table
lists all test-family loss counts and separates the observed diagnostic
mechanisms. Nonpositive curvature rejects a nonminimum; the remaining rows
have an available Newton calculation but can still be uncertified or excluded
by the runaway rule. These diagnostics alone do not establish a basin mechanism.

```{r loss-summary}
z <- loss[loss$role == "test", ]
z$Curvature <- as.integer(z$newton_status == "nonpositive_curvature")
z$Runaway <- as.integer(z$runaway)
z$Other <- 1L - z$Curvature - z$Runaway
q <- aggregate(cbind(Curvature, Runaway, Other) ~ family + candidate, z, sum)
q <- q[order(q$family, q$candidate), ]
tab(data.frame(Family = fam[q$family], Candidate = arms[q$candidate],
               `Nonpositive curvature` = q$Curvature, Runaway = q$Runaway,
               `Other uncertified stops` = q$Other, check.names = FALSE))
```

The default's attainable constrained $\times 0.01$ failures fell from 2,677
on 2026-09-27 to `r f0(x001("default"))` on fresh draws. This supports the
TASK-131 units fix, not a claim that all constrained fitting failures are gone.

Certified test fits with chart extent above 1000 fell from 287 to
`r f0(pole("default"))` for the default and from 510 to
`r f0(pole("layered_port"))` for layered PORT. The frozen `runaways.csv`
locates 29 default and 88 layered-PORT cases in equality-constrained models,
where std.lv transport is unsupported. It also records two default cases in
Boomsma ($\lambda=1$) and three layered-PORT cases in engineering/15
($\lambda=0.25$). Thus the remaining cases are **not exclusively
 equality-constrained**. The summary tables do not give their transport status;
raw rows are not present in this checkout. Both L-BFGS arms have zero certified
test fits above 1000. The scoring continues to reject all such points.

## Dated history: 2026-09-27

The original run at seed base 2026092701 retained the default, although it
scored only 85,679 test fits and candidates gained in the constrained family.
The default failed 2,677 attainable constrained $\times 0.01$ fits; the
native fallback was in the wrong units. Certified chart extent > 1000 occurred
287 times for the default and 510 times for layered PORT. These findings
motivated TASK-131 and TASK-137 before fresh confirmation. The original
summaries and every loss remain in `results/barrier-ml/2026-09-27/`.
The inspected layered-start failures suggested attraction toward factor
disappearance; that interpretation is historical diagnostic evidence, not a
mechanism independently established for every fresh loss.

## Caveats

The run covers complete-data ML, the determinacy penalty, two weights
($0.25$ and $1$), and the registered populations and unit transforms. It does
not cover FIML, multi-group models or the joint penalty. Population-start
witnesses define attainability and the best-known objective, not a proof of a
global minimum. The chart bound of 1000 is a registered scoring rule, not proof
of nonattainment. Equality-constrained transport remains open.

The 2026-10-09 summaries were frozen at `2fbec812`; metadata records the
clean library source `dd6325ad` and seed base 2026100901. This is a fresh paired
confirmation after fixes, rather than a draw-by-draw comparison to September.

## Reproduce

The rerun used simbox with 14 single-threaded workers and took about six
minutes. Rendering reads only the frozen CSVs.

```sh
cd experiments/decisions/02-barrier-defaults
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --run-id 2026-10-09 \
  --seed-base 2026100901 --workers 14
Rscript run_experiment.R --run-id 2026-10-09 --seed-base 2026100901 --summarize
quarto render report.qmd --to html
```
